subject: sociology
title: The Sociologist's Toolkit
welcome_lead: Meet the methods sociologists use to study society, from snap surveys to deep undercover work.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on primary, secondary, quantitative and qualitative research methods.
final_note: You can now match a method to a research aim — that is the heart of the methods exam.

concepts.def: Does the data really measure what it claims?
Would the same method give the same result again?

walkthroughs.body_html: Primary data comes from your own questionnaire, interview or observation. Secondary data uses what already exists: ONS statistics, diaries, newspapers, school records. Primary is fresh; secondary is fast and cheap.

Quantitative methods like closed questionnaires give numbers you can graph. Qualitative methods like unstructured interviews give rich meaning. Positivists prefer quantitative; interpretivists prefer qualitative.
Use the acronym PERVERT: Practical, Ethical, Reliability, Validity, Examples, Representativeness, Theoretical (positivist or interpretivist). Hit each one in a methods answer.
